title: How Many Laps In A Formula 1 Race?
description: A Formula 1 race can run anywhere from 44 to 78 laps, since every race is built around a fixed minimum distance rather than a…
fullText:
A Formula 1 race can run anywhere from 44 to 78 laps, since every race is built around a fixed minimum distance rather than a fixed lap count. The shortest lap counts belong to the longest circuits, and the longest lap counts belong to the shortest ones.

The 2026 calendar spans 44 laps at Spa-Francorchamps, the longest circuit at 7.004km, to 78 laps at Monaco, the shortest at 3.337km.

Every race other than Monaco is set at the fewest complete laps that exceed 305km; Monaco alone runs to a shorter 260km minimum.

Sprint races cover roughly 100km regardless of venue, which works out to 19 laps at Miami’s Autodrome in 2026.

Lap counts on the 2026 calendar range from 44 at the longest end to 78 at the shortest, because every race is built to a minimum distance rather than a fixed number of laps. Spa-Francorchamps, at 7.004km the longest circuit F1 visits, needs only 44 laps to clear its 305km minimum, the exact lap count confirmed at this year’s Belgian Grand Prix. Monaco, at 3.337km the shortest circuit on the calendar, needs 78 laps to reach its own, shorter 260km minimum, the lap count run at the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix. Most circuits fall somewhere between those two extremes: Silverstone, at 5.891km, runs 52 laps for the 2026 British Grand Prix, a typical mid-calendar figure neither extreme comes close to, a spread that reflects just how differently Formula 1’s circuits around the world are laid out.

Formula 1 sets race distance first and works the lap count backwards from it. Under Article B2.5.2 of the FIA’s Sporting Regulations, a Grand Prix distance is fixed at the fewest number of complete laps that exceeds 305km, with Monaco alone permitted a shorter 260km minimum because of its unusually tight, slow layout. Monaco’s own numbers show how the rule lands in practice: at 3.337km a lap, 77 laps covers only 256.95km, still short of the 260km minimum, so the race runs to 78 laps and 260.29km instead. The same arithmetic applies at Madrid’s new Madring circuit, debuting on the 2026 calendar: at 5.416km a lap, 56 laps falls short of 305km at 303.3km, so the race is set at 57 laps and 308.7km, the first lap count to clear the line, and the distance Madrid’s organisers have confirmed for the race. Every circuit’s lap count is simply that same calculation run against its own lap length, and the rounding is always upward rather than to the nearest lap: a circuit whose lap length does not divide neatly into 305km will always finish a few kilometres over the minimum rather than under it, since a race can clear the line early but never fall short of it. Lap counts are recalculated whenever a circuit’s layout changes, which is why a shortened or lengthened track can shift a race’s lap count from one season to the next even though the underlying distance rule never moves.

Monaco runs the most laps of any race on the 2026 calendar, 78 laps of its 3.337km street circuit, because its shorter permitted distance and tight lap length combine to push the count higher than anywhere else F1 races. At the other end, the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps runs the fewest, just 44 laps, since Spa’s 7.004km is the longest lap on the calendar and clears the standard 305km minimum in far fewer trips around the circuit. Most other circuits sit well between these two extremes, since few tracks approach either Monaco’s tight, technical layout or Spa’s sweeping length.

A sprint race covers roughly 100km regardless of venue, a fixed distance rather than a fixed lap count, so the number of laps still depends on the circuit. At Miami International Autodrome, one of six sprint venues on the 2026 calendar alongside Shanghai, Montreal, Silverstone, Zandvoort and Singapore, that works out to 19 laps. Each sprint weekend runs its own separate qualifying session to set the sprint grid, entirely independent of the qualifying session that sets Sunday’s Grand Prix grid, so a driver’s sprint lap count and race lap count are decided by two different sessions rather than one. Sprint races run to a 60 minute time limit and typically finish in around 30 minutes, far shorter than the lap counts and durations that apply to the Grand Prix held the same weekend.

Not always. A race can be stopped before its scheduled distance is reached, most often by a red flag for extreme weather or a serious incident, and if it isn’t restarted, the classification is taken from the last completed lap rather than the original target. Points for an incomplete race now follow a sliding scale rather than a flat half share: full points require at least 75 per cent of the scheduled distance, several reduced tiers apply below that, and nothing is awarded at all unless the leader has completed at least two green-flag racing laps. The most extreme example remains the 2021 Belgian Grand Prix, red-flagged after just three laps behind the safety car and classified at under a single full lap of racing. A suspended race restarts only inside a strict window of two hours of racing within a three-hour total, and once that outer clock runs out, the classification stands wherever the field stopped.

title: Andoni Iraola reveals concern over new Liverpool defensive signing
description: Liverpool Team News: Gravenberch, Isak and Wirtz Set for Leeds Friendly ReturnLiverpool will finally get a proper look at three major names in Chicago. Ryan Gravenberch, Alexander Isak and Florian Wir...
fullText:
Liverpool will finally get a proper look at three major names in Chicago. Ryan Gravenberch, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz are all expected to feature against Leeds United at Soldier Field, with Andoni Iraola confirming the plan ahead of Sunday’s pre-season fixture.

That matters. These are not fringe players needing a token run-out. They are key parts of Liverpool’s build for the new season, and after arriving late to the USA camp, the head coach wants them on the pitch now, even if only in controlled spells.

Iraola was clear enough: “With Florian, Ryan and Alex, they’ve been the ones arriving late.” He added, “I think we’ve been cautious in terms of giving them the time to reach to the level where the others are, because they’ve been training for two weeks before them, but my idea is that the three of them will play the last game against Leeds.”

No mystery here. Liverpool are not going to overload any of them. Iraola said, “Probably we’ll have to restrict their minutes. We still have another three weeks before the start of the season where they will play more, we can push them more.” That is sensible, especially at this stage of pre-season.

There was also a telling line from the head coach, and it goes to the point of these friendlies. “But I think we need them to start as soon as possible because sometimes they have to make the mistakes now, so we can have time to correct them.” That is honest coaching. Better the errors arrive in July than when the Premier League starts.

One player still in doubt is Jeremy Jacquet. The summer arrival missed the games against Sunderland and Wrexham after suffering what was described as “discomfort” in training, and Liverpool are not forcing the issue.

Iraola said, “With Jeremy we still don’t know if it’s worth it or not to put him in against Leeds.” He also made the wider situation plain: “He did the first part of the pre-season, let’s say, very well. Now he’s feeling some discomfort, so we don’t want to rush him.”

That caution is understandable. Jacquet has had a long spell without playing, and Liverpool are already light in senior central defence. As Iraola put it, “He comes from a lot of months without playing. And obviously I would like to try with him with Virgil [van Dijk] when he recovers, because with the injury of Joe [Gomez] we’ve been without senior centre-backs. But we have to be careful with Jeremy, yes.”

There is better news elsewhere. Stefan Bajcetic is effectively back in full training, while Wataru Endo is also closing in on a return. Iraola said, “Stefan is training basically fully with the team. Wataru has started training more progressively but [is] very close to being ready.”

There is even a target for Endo’s comeback. “I hope Wata can play probably against Monaco. He should be able to have some minutes.” For more on Liverpool’s latest pre-season updates, details were first outlined here. For now, the headline is simple, Gravenberch, Isak and Wirtz are set to play, and that gives Liverpool’s pre-season some proper substance.

title: Fans Left Incredulous After Tigers’ Tarik Skubal Lands With Dodgers
description: As the saying goes, the rich simply get richer.That’s the case right now for the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers, who have shown they have every intention of a three-peat thanks to their acquisition of back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winning pitcher Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers late on Saturday evening.In […] The post Fans Left Incredulous After Tigers’ Tarik Skubal Lands With Dodgers appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
As the saying goes, the rich simply get richer.

That’s the case right now for the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers, who have shown they have every intention of a three-peat thanks to their acquisition of back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winning pitcher Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers late on Saturday evening.

In return for Skubal, who missed several weeks of action this season after undergoing a non-invasive surgical procedure to remove a loose body from his throwing arm, the Tigers received outfielder Zyhir Hope, right-hander River Ryan and right-hander Brady Smith.

Unfortunately for the Tigers, it brings to a close another era of having one of the best pitchers in baseball as part of their rotation, just as when they traded away Justin Verlander in 2017 and lost Max Scherzer to free agency in 2015.

And now, fans everywhere are reacting to the news of Skubal’s acquisition by the Dodgers.

The Dodgers already hold the highest luxury tax payroll in Major League Baseball at approximately $421 million, which has garnered significant criticism from fans of smaller market teams as being an unfair playing advantage.

Nevertheless, the Dodgers remain compliant with current MLB rules, and fans believe that it’s a major reason why baseball could be heading for a lockout in 2027.

This fan said, “Thank you to the Dodgers for the Great MLB Lockout of 2027 🤢”

Another fan exclaimed, “Dodgers literally ruined the sport of baseball. Brewers probably offered but dodgers inflation strikes once again and Skubal probably didn’t want to go to brewers.”

Ben Verlander, the brother of Justin, wrote, “Oh my god. Tarik Skubal to the Dodgers. Is it possible to not be able to believe something while also feeling it was inevitable the whole time?”

MLB Insider George Jarjour wrote in part, “Uh oh. The Dodgers just added Tarik Skubal, the reigning two-time Cy Young winner. The Dodgers already had Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Mookie Betts, Freddie Feeman etc. Four months from now, the CBA expires. I said this trade would be the last piece of evidence the owners need to shut the sport down, and it just happened.”

This fan felt the Tigers should have gotten 

Finally, this fan said, “Enjoy nights like this while they last. Deals like Skubal to LA are exactly what shoves the sport toward a lockout, and the CBA dies after 2026. This might be the best baseball we get before a work stoppage.”

Skubal, who is the back to back American League Cy Young Award winner, will now attempt to help the Dodgers win the World Series for what would be a third straight season.

If the Dodgers are able to do so, they’d be the first MLB club to three-peat since the New York Yankees did so from 1998 to 2000.

So far this season, Skubal has amassed a 7-5 record with a 2.79 ERA and a 0.91 WHIP.

title: LeBron James’ emergency plan if he loses $1.4 billion fortune involves two ultra-rare rookie cards
description: LeBron James is the first active NBA player to become a billionaire, but he has some contingencies not in his official net worth to keep him afloat if he loses his fortune. LeBron is one of the greatest basketball players of all time, but he also might be one of the best basketball businessmen ever, with both titles being contested with Michael Jordan.
fullText:
LeBron James is the first active NBA player to become a billionaire, but he has some contingencies not in his official net worth to keep him afloat if he loses his fortune.

LeBron is one of the greatest basketball players of all time, but he also might be one of the best basketball businessmen ever, with both titles being contested with Michael Jordan.

James has a reported net worth of $1.4 billion according to Forbes, but he has two pieces of prized memorabilia that don’t factor into that worth.

James was doing an interview with Topps where they discussed the rarest cards to have sold with his likeness on it, with James revealing he might have his own $5.2 million rookie edition card in a vault.

“I think my rookie card sold for the most, but I heard it’s like crazy. I happen to maybe have one or two of those cards locked in a vault somewhere. So, just in case I ever fall on hard times, I’m good.”

James joked about how those rookie cards will help him get back on his feet if he ever falls on hard times, but he has more than enough levers to pull.

Most of his game-worn memorabilia from major highlights of his career could be more valuable than a rookie Topps card, but if you put it all together, James could add $100 million to his net worth just by putting an actual value on these items.

James’ $5.2 million 2003 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Rookie Patch Autograph card actually cost $6.4 million to the new owner after all fees and taxes were accounted for.

If James were to sell his own personal version of the card, it’d be far more valuable because it is a verifiable belonging of James, not just a card that came out of a pack.

The most expensive sports card of all time cost $12.9 million in August 2025, a 2007–08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Autograph with both Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant.

Cards with LeBron as a rookie are bound to become more valuable in the coming years, especially after he retires from the sport.

The billionaire James can afford to play on minimum NBA contracts in his twilight due to his shrewd off-court success, so it’s unlikely he’d suddenly lose his fortune and need to sell cards and memorabilia to restart his life.

title: Sooo ... About Last Night
description: Last night (Sat., Aug. 1, 2026), Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) ventured forth to Belgrade Arena in Belgrade, Serbia, for UFC Belgrade. Though the card was centered around “The Doctor,” Uros Medic, in his home country debut, the UFC’s first visit to Serbia will be remembered for a wild run of finishes to start the night! […]
fullText:
Last night (Sat., Aug. 1, 2026), Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) ventured forth to Belgrade Arena in Belgrade, Serbia, for UFC Belgrade. Though the card was centered around “The Doctor,” Uros Medic, in his home country debut, the UFC’s first visit to Serbia will be remembered for a wild run of finishes to start the night! There was no shortage of action in this entertaining event, which proved a lovely way to wake up for western fight fans.

Let’s take a closer look at the best performances and highlight finishes of the evening:

Everybody knows Medic intends to destroy his opposition with the first punch of the fight — that doesn’t make it any easier to deal with!

Daniel Rodriguez showed up looking fit in his return and tried to establish his jab and low kick early on. That’s fundamentally sound, but the speed difference was too great. Less than 30 seconds into the fight, Rodriguez stepped forward to jab, and before he even let the punch loose from its chamber, Medic unleashed a three-punch combination. The opening left landed heavily on the jaw, and the next couple punches sent Rodriguez flying backward. “D-Rod” was hurt badly, and Medic jumped on him with ground strikes to secure the quick KO win.

Belgrade went absolutely wild in one of the most memorable moments of 2026.

Where does Medic go from here? He’s on quite the tear of quick knockouts, but he also hasn’t really proven that he’s solidified the grappling holes exposed in earlier UFC losses. As such, a Top 10 opponent who can test that aspect of his game feels appropriate, as we can then evaluate if Medic has truly developed into an elite title threat.

How about Sean Brady or Gabriel Bonfim?

The 205-pound field is wide open. The champion is injured, most of the top contenders are stagnant, and half of the division has fled up to Heavyweight, which is somehow even weaker. The division is in a fairly dire state, but Navajo Stirling is an exception.

Stirling was an attractive pickup right away. A 6’4” former pro kickboxer training with City Kickboxing sure sounds like a recipe for UFC success. Though he won his first three UFC bouts, they never really left second gear, and Stirling didn’t show much aggression or finishing instinct in the process. A 3-0 start is undeniably good, but it was a bit underwhelming.

2026 has marked a level up for Stirling. After stopping both Bruno Lopes and Ion Cutelaba, Stirling just dispatched an actually good fighter via knockout! Jan Blachowicz may be shopworn at 43, but he’s still a remarkably tough out for most of the division. He hasn’t been knocked out since 2019, yet a Stirling 1-2 sat him down hard midway through the first.

It’s important to take a step back and realize this was only Stirling’s 11th pro MMA fight. He started this year at just 8-0. The 28-year-old Kiwi is just now getting settled into the sport, and his newfound confidence is allowing his skill to flourish and producing much more exciting results.

Stirling walks away from this win already in title contention, and the best is yet to come from this rising talent.

Three fights into his UFC career, Tofiq Musayev is exceeding expectations.

Don’t get me wrong, serious fans knew Musayev well as an incredibly explosive and dangerous finisher. Sadly, it felt like Musayev’s best days were behind him by the time he signed with the UFC. He (arguably) peaked in 2019 when he won four fights over tough competition to win the RIZIN Lightweight Grand Prix, extending his win streak to 15. After a two year layoff, Musayev returned to lose two of his next three by finish, and he didn’t make his UFC debut until 2025 at the age of 35.

It all felt too late. Musayev was picked up solely because the UFC was heading to his home country of Azerbaijan, and his quick tap to Myktybek Orolbai at the first UFC Baku event seemed to confirm that he wasn’t long for the Lightweight ranks.

Instead, Musayev righted the ship! He went to war with Ignacio Bahamondes five months ago in an incredible fight that booted “La Jaula” from the 155-pound rankings and proved there was still gas left in the tank. Last night, he faced the battle-hardened Ludovit Klein in a highly anticipated matchup and once more demonstrated that Musayev has a lot left to offer.

Sometimes, high-level fights are decided by who finds the range first. In this case, Musayev found an early avenue to success in the form of clattering inside shin kicks. Those kicks hurt both men, but they effectively knocked Klein way out of his stance, limiting his ability to counter and allowing Musayev to explode forward with further swings.

Defeating Bahamondes and Klein back-to-back is no joke! At 36, Musayev has earned his Top 15 ranking, and he deserves his chance to make a run at the top.

Michael Oliveira is something special.

“PQD” debuted last night on the undercard versus Oban Elliott, a solid Welterweight veteran with a good mix of skills. The Brazilian — who appears to be sculpted by the same stoneworker that crafted Yoel Romero from marble — was patient in his attack, feinting his way forward and calmly withdrawing away from Elliott’s combinations. As soon as he decided to unleash, his power made itself known: a snapping jab floored Elliott!

Oliveira’s vicious display of power was not a one-off event. He soon sent Elliott flying with a straight right, following up with a nasty series of ground strikes as Elliott desperately tried to flee for safety.

Young and electric, the former Brazilian paratrooper has the look of a star. I am slightly worried about whether the 6’1” slugger will continue to make the Welterweight cut for years to come without issue, but that’s a potential problem for tomorrow.

Robert Valentin defeats Dusko Todorovic via first-round guillotine: If you like silly grappling fun, this is the bout for you! Valentin vs. Todorovic was an aggressive collision of okay jiu-jitsu vs. okay wrestling. Valentin started off strong by reversing Todorovic with a high-elbow guillotine attempt. Then, after some control time, Valentin placed himself in a double leg along the fence and nearly got himself Von Flue choked by hanging onto the neck for too long. The scrambles continued with a big hip bridge, a switch, and eventually another guillotine choke — this one sealed the deal.

Gilbert Urbina defeats Vlasto Cepo via first-round knockout: Cepo fought with way too much recklessness and nervous energy. He was incredibly sloppy in his initial surge of aggression, whereas Urbina kept his composure. In the face of wild swings, Urbina actually did really well to move his head and counter with intercepting knees and elbows. As Cepo started to lose a little steam from his own sprinting, Urbina clipped him with a jab and sent him to the canvas — that’s all she wrote! Though Cepo is known for brawling, the atmosphere of fighting in his home country for his UFC debut clearly made him a bit too eager.

Noah Gugnon defeats Milos Janicic via first-round rear naked choke: Was the main card opener disappointing or impressive? That’s up for debate. Gugnon injured Janicic with the very first low kick he threw, and then the wobbly Janicic was hardly able to defend himself. It was effectively a flawless debut from the 25-year-old Swede, but we also didn’t get to see him tested. Conversely, we cannot judge Janicic too harshly, as the professional kickboxer with a 19-4 MMA record is not usually crippled by the first kick of the fight.

Bogdan Grad defeats Dennis Buzukja via second-round arm triangle (highlights): It’s a shame when an entertaining fight ends with a lackluster finish. Grad lived up to his nonstop wrestler reputation in round one, spinning wildly then grinding away with takedowns. All that grappling slowed both men in round two, however, allowing Buzukja to get his boxing going and land some clean combinations. In the final minute of the second, Grad threw a right hand and rolled into a beautiful double leg along the fence — textbook MMA wrestling. From top position, he started attacking an arm triangle … and did Buzukja tap? Maybe! It was hard to tell whether Buzukja was simply trying to frame off the hip or pull off the infamous “Brazilian tap,” a half-hearted tap intended to trick the opponent into easing up pressure. Either way, the referee halted the contest, and we all know MMA commissions are unlikely to take any appeal seriously. Buzukja may be pissed, but the result will stand.

Mateusz Rebecki defeats Kyle Prepolec via first-round knockout: It’s great to see Rebecki pick up a win without traveling to the seventh circle of Hell in the process. Rebecki is somewhat infamous for failing to utilize the proper game plan, but the Polish standout didn’t waste long before turning to his wrestling here. He ground Prepolec easily and straight up bullied the Canadian veteran on the canvas for the early finish. On that note: is there a better 0-5 UFC fighter than Prepolec? He’s a skilled striker, but no wins in two UFC stints is a rough run of luck.

Nina Milosevic defeats Hailey Cowan via first-round knockout: How often do we see elite body punching in women’s MMA? Jessica Andrade is the only one who comes to mind, though she was guilty of head-hunting too much. In a single fight, Milosevic has already placed herself on that shortlist courtesy of two nasty straight rights to the breadbasket that folded her opponent. Women’s Bantamweight has been horribly stagnant in recent years, so it’s lovely to see a newcomer on the right side of 30 with finishing instincts make a successful debut.

Jovan Leka defeats Alexander Poppeck via first-round knockout (highlights): Is it a bit of softball matchmaking to book a hometown Heavyweight against a 205-pounder? Of course. Still, Leka had to get the job done, and the massive 24-year-old did just that! Midway through the first round, Leka unleashed an absolutely ripping body kick that landed with the crack of a baseball bat. Poppeck crumbled, and the big boy division suddenly has a new prospect on its hands.

Stephanie Luciano defeats Marina Spasic via first-round rear naked choke (highlights): Luciano looked sharp here against her debuting foe. Her jab was effective early, and then she timed a takedown well to move into mount. A few ground strikes convinced Spasic to turn her back, and that was a wrap! Now 3-1 in the Octagon, the 26-year-old Brazilian is starting to look like a solid Strawweight prospect.

title: Bayern Munich U-17 season preview with Lars Bender: Friendlies, transfers, start of season, goals and more…
description: The U-17s have signed a big name.
fullText:
Last season’s Bayern Munich U-17s head coach Leonard Haas has moved up to the U-19s, meaning he has had to be replaced. In a shocking turn, that replacement has turned out to be Lars Bender, who possesses over a decade of experience playing in the Bundesliga. Furthermore, the former Bayer Leverkusen player has had experience managing in the fourth division of German football, leading SV Wacker Burghausen into 51 games. How Bayern secured him as a manager is anyone’s guess.

Just because Bender is a huge name does not mean he will be a success, though. First he will need to showcase his mettle by working to improve on last season’s slightly disappointing results. The team fared excellently in the first phase of the U-17 Bundesliga season, but blew exclusively hot or cold in the second phase, scraping to the next phase before unceremoniously being dumped out in the Round of 16.

Bayern’s official website provides a good look at what lies ahead, before the season even truly begin, starting with a review of the coaching staff:

Lars Bender, a former Bundesliga professional and national team player with extensive experience, will take over as head coach. He has also coached at both the youth level (assistant coach for Germany’s U16 and U17 teams, head coach of Unterhaching’s U17 team) and at the senior level (SV Wacker Burghausen). The coaching team is completed by Philipp Deppner, previously assistant coach of the U19s, and Benjamin Kauffmann, most recently head coach of the U14s, who will now serve as assistant coaches.

Bender: “I am very satisfied with the start and I am looking forward to getting to know the guys gradually. I am also taking enough time to have individual talks with each of them. You can feel a great willingness and excitement for the time ahead from everyone.”

Naturally, preseason is filled with a lot of intensive training and multiple friendlies. The Bavarians have schedule 3 friendlies thus far, as well as two tournaments in the Bundesliga Cup and the Red&Gold Global Trophy tournament, and will go through an intensive preseason before the season official begins on the weekend of August 9th (to be terminated more exactly on a later date:

July 4 : vs Stuttgarter Kickers U-17s (8-1 win)

July 18-19: U-17 Bundesliga Cup

August 1: vs Slavia Prague U-17s

August 4-6: Red&Gold Global Trophy tournament

Weekend of August 9: Season start

If one is not familiar with the format of Germany’s U-17 and U-19 leagues, one can read about it here. In short, though, there are three phases to each season. The first phase consists of 14 league matches in groups of 8, with Bayern set to play against each of the 7 opponents twice. This season, the first phase starts on August 9 and ends on the weekend around December 6th (just like the U-19s).

Bayern have been drawn into Group C with these other teams:

A main criteria for choosing teams is how close each team is to the other, which is why Bayern have been drawn to play against the likes of 1859+1 Munich and Unterhaching again.

Bender has this to say about the opponents, via Bayern’s website: “It’s a good group – we had already prepared for this or a similar constellation. For us, the focus is now on preparation before we look forward to the preliminary round in the youth league.”

The transfer window is now open and one external transfer has been made in VFB Stuttgart talent Kemi Seudie. This is a list of all the players currently registered for the U-17s. Of course, there will be changes to this list. There is every chance new players/returning loanees will arrive over the course of preseason or even after the season has already started. Or a few of these players could be let go, loaned out or promoted to the U-19s/U-23s over the course of the window. Furthermore, there are multiple players out injured that are listed as part of the squad yet cannot participate in any of the training sessions or games.

Still, at the time of writing, here is the full squad list:

Timo Dachgruber, Tim Ebert, Atakan Etüz, Noah Fichtl, Niklas Herber, Thibault Maspimby, Joyce Nduka, Skender Nuraj, Lamar Rama, Tim Schreyer

Roko Ciglar, Franz Hoffmann, Maximilian Mahr, Tarik Mujic, Noah Rieber, Kemi Seudie, Deni Zubovic

Daniel Abade, Isuf Hiseni, Florent Krasniqi. Linus Ludwig, Veded Turbic

Immediately, the squad seems very balanced. There could be a need to add one more forward and move on one or two midfielders, but otherwise the squad looks strong heading into the season.

At the time of writing, Bender’s men played three friendlies.

8-1 vs Stuttgarter Kickers U-17s

Unlike the U-19s, the U-17s are in just one competition: The U-17 Bundesliga. The goal will be to prioritize youth development, of course, but also to surpass the Round of 16 exit from last season.

title: Ajinkya Rahane retirement: Newly retired ex-India captain to receive hefty monthly pension from BCCI
description: Following his retirement from international cricket, former India captain Ajinkya Rahane is eligible for a monthly pension from the BCCI. Find out the exact amount and benefits.
fullText:
Ajinkya Rahane retirement: Newly retired ex-India captain to receive hefty monthly pension from BCCI originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Ajinkya Rahane retired from cricket and is set to receive BCCI pension benefits.

Revised 2022 pension scheme entitles him to a hefty monthly amount.

Pension pauses if Rahane takes up an official BCCI administrative role.

Ajinkya Rahane brought the curtain down on his playing career on July 30, closing out a journey that included leading India to a landmark Border-Gavaskar Trophy win in Australia during the 2020-21 series as stand-in skipper.

As the seasoned batter transitions into life after playing days, he'll naturally look toward fresh sources of income, and in that regard, he can count on the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

Back in 2022, the BCCI overhauled its pension structure for cricketers who had hung up their boots. This change was rolled out during Sourav Ganguly's time as BCCI President.

MORE: Who will be the KKR captain in IPL 2027? Three names who can replace Ajinkya Rahane

Given his tally of 85 Test appearances, Rahane qualifies for the board's highest pension bracket.

Players with a similar level of experience previously received Rs 50,000 every month, but that figure was bumped up to Rs 70,000 monthly four years ago under the revised policy.

As a result, Rahane will now draw a fixed Rs 70,000 each month going forward.

"It is extremely important that the financial well-being of our former cricketers is taken care of. The players remain the lifeline and, as a Board, it is our duty to be by their side once their playing days are over. The umpires have been unsung heroes, and the BCCI truly values their contribution," Ganguly said at the time.

MORE: Why Bhuvneshwar Kumar could make it to India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad?

Rahane hasn't yet spelt out exactly what his post-retirement path will involve.

He has, however, indicated an interest in mentoring upcoming cricketers as the next phase of his journey.

It's worth noting that his pension eligibility comes with a caveat: should he take on any official position within the BCCI, whether as an administrator or a coach, his pension payments would be paused for the duration of that role, since he would then be drawing a salary for those responsibilities instead.

title: Hardik Pandya new look: MI captain appears in new avatar amid IPL trade rumours and India return
description: Hardik Pandya was spotted in a new avatar after he visited the Tirumala temple.
fullText:
Hardik Pandya new look: MI captain appears in new avatar amid IPL trade rumours and India return originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Hardik Pandya shaves his head, visits Tirumala temple amid injury recovery buzz.

All-rounder completes rehab, eyes India comeback after months on the sidelines.

Mumbai Indians deny active trade talks despite swirling exit speculation.

Hardik Pandya turned heads with a striking new appearance after he was photographed with a completely bald head during a visit to the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala, where he offered prayers alongside his girlfriend Mahieka Sharma.

The couple took part in the temple's Suprabhatam Seva, regarded as one of its most sacred morning rituals, before seeking blessings at the shrine of Lord Venkateswara.

Devotees often offer their hair at the temple as a gesture of devotion and gratitude, which might be the reason for Pandya's decision to go bald.

MORE: MI deny trade talks amid rumours of Hardik Pandya and Suryakumar Yadav leaving ahead of IPL 2027

The temple trip arrives at a crucial moment in Pandya's career, as he continues working his way back from injury. He has been out of action since he suffered a back injury followed by a thigh problem after IPL 2026 concluded.

Reports indicate he has now completed his rehabilitation and return-to-play protocols at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. This puts him back in the frame for India's upcoming white-ball fixtures.

Pandya has already missed the limited-overs series against Afghanistan, India's ODI and T20I tour of England, and the white-ball leg in Zimbabwe. In fact, he hasn't featured in a single competitive match since leading Mumbai Indians through IPL 2026, a campaign that ended without a playoff spot for the five-time champions.

MORE: SKY set to leave MI: Mumbai Indians likely to make Tilak new captain - Report

Mumbai Indians have stepped in to address growing chatter around their roster, denying that any trade discussions are currently underway despite persistent rumours linking both Pandya and Suryakumar Yadav with potential departures.

The franchise is conducting a thorough post-season review following another underwhelming IPL 2026 campaign, and their statement comes on the back of reports suggesting a major squad reshuffle could be in the works.

Chennai Super Kings have been named as a possible landing spot for captain Pandya, with Rajasthan Royals, Kolkata Knight Riders, and Delhi Capitals also reportedly weighing up interest in the all-rounder. Yadav's name has also featured prominently in the speculation, with Tilak Varma tipped as the likely candidate to succeed him as captain should he move on.

MORE: Hardik Pandya trade: MI want CSK duo as part of swap deal

Addressing the rumours directly, an MI spokesperson firmly denied any ongoing negotiations, telling Sportstar that the post-season review was still in progress and that every aspect of the team was under evaluation.

"Our post-season review is currently on, and we are looking into all aspects of the team. Contrary to reports, we are not engaged in conversations about player trades; the same is only possible once the review is complete," the spokesperson said.

"A range of options and ideas are being evaluated, which require time; hence, no decisions have been made."

Pandya's shaved head might just be a personal choice tied to his temple visit, but the timing makes it hard not to read deeper meaning into it. It comes right as speculation swirls around his MI future and his international comeback hangs in the balance.

The image feels symbolic of someone stripping things back and starting fresh, whether that's intentional or not.

What's clear is that Pandya finds himself at a genuine crossroads. His fitness has been a persistent concern for over a year now, and missing an extended stretch of international cricket only adds pressure heading into his return.

Meanwhile, MI's insistence that no trades are happening doesn't erase the fact that reports keep surfacing from multiple credible sources, suggesting there's at least some truth to the smoke even if there's no fire yet.

For a player who has spent years as one of Indian cricket's most valuable assets, both as a finisher and an all-rounder, this period feels less about optics and more about proving his body can hold up again. Whether he stays at MI or moves elsewhere matters far less right now than whether he can actually get back on the field consistently.

title: 6 takeaways from first week of Commanders' training camp
description: The Commanders have been on the practice field for a few days now. Here are six thoughts as they head into Week 2.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders began training camp last Wednesday and have three practices in the books before getting a day off on Sunday. When Washington returns to the practice field on Monday, players will be in pads for the first time this summer.

Over the first few days of camp, we've sensed a common theme: the defense is ahead of the offense. That's not to say the offense has been bad, but the defense usually looks better in the early stages of camp. Remember, the Commanders have a new offensive coordinator (David Blough) and defensive coordinator (Daronte Jones) who are employing new schemes.

So, with Washington having a day off on Sunday, it feels like the perfect time to look back at the first few days of training camp. Here are six takeaways from the Commanders' first week of camp.

Early in camp, Jones is throwing a variety of looks at Jayden Daniels and Washington's offense. It has sometimes been a challenge, especially for the interior of the Commanders' offensive line. At times, Daniels has had to hold the ball too long, which would be a sack in a real game. However, Daniels has improved each day and hasn't had a bad practice yet. It's terrific practice for him. Remember, he's playing under center exclusively for the first time in a while, and in a new offensive scheme. Every rep for Daniels against multiple and varied looks is a win for the Commanders.

On the first day of practice, Nick Allegretti went down with an injury. Head coach Dan Quinn said Allegretti was dealing with a calf strain and would probably miss a week. In the meantime, Julian Good-Jones is the No. 1 center, with rookie sixth-round pick Matt Gulbin as the backup. It's led the coaches to have other players, such as Brandon Coleman and Trent Scott, take snaps.

While having backups get some valuable snaps early in camp would normally be a good thing, it's very concerning. Allegretti, while a reliable veteran lineman, is no sure thing at center. He's mostly played guard in the NFL. He has played center at times, but has never established himself there. The problem here is that this is a new offense, and Daniels is adjusting to playing under center more consistently. When you throw all of that into a pot, you reach a worrisome conclusion. It doesn't matter how great the rest of the offensive line is; if Washington struggles at center, that's a huge problem.

We've written multiple times this offseason that center was more of a concern than wide receiver. The Commanders chose not to add another veteran to compete with Allegretti. With all due respect to Good-Jones, Washington can't go into Week 1 where it's only one snap away from a catastrophe along the offensive line.

Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic had people talking on Thursday when she made the following post on X.

My assessment of the first two days of Commanders camp: pic.twitter.com/RtTE7ELg5H

— Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) July 30, 2026

For those wondering, Jhabvala posted a GIF of free-agent wide receiver Stefon Diggs, indicating that Washington's receivers not named Terry McLaurin didn't have a huge start to training camp. It's not like they've been bad, but there have been issues creating separation. The depth is really good, at least compared to last year, but there is still a glaring need for a No. 2 opposite McLaurin. Diggs remains a free agent, too. GM Adam Peters could be waiting to see how Blough's scheme can create separation, or whether players like Treylon Burks, Antonio Williams, or Dyami Brown give him the confidence not to make a move.

Remember when some criticized the Commanders for giving Oweh a four-year, $100 million deal? In the early days of camp, Oweh has stood out in a big way. He's big, fast, twitchy, and while he's fast, it's not just straight-line speed. Oweh can move side to side with ease and made an impressive play against Daniels on the first day of camp. Oweh and fellow newcomer K'Lavon Chaisson should have an excellent year if they stay healthy. Oweh is coming off his two best seasons and could have a huge year in Jones' scheme in 2026.

Veteran cornerback Rasul Douglas just signed with the Commanders last month. On Wednesday, he took to the podium and introduced himself. When asked what he brings to the defense, here's how Douglas responded: "Turnovers. That's what I do. I get turnovers, so I'm looking to add that to the squad."

Not only did Douglas have an interception early in camp, but he's always around the ball. It's remarkable that a solid veteran cornerback who has played well in recent years was still available. He went from not having a team one month ago to likely being a key part of Washington's secondary in 2026. The cornerback room suddenly looks much better and deeper after the addition of Douglas.

Terry McLaurin essentially missed all of training camp last summer due to contentious contract negotiations with the Commanders. McLaurin is a team-first guy who doesn't like to miss anything. The team felt his absence last year. It was even worse when he missed seven games with an injury. McLaurin is Washington's No. 1 receiver, but he's also the ultimate leader, teammate and mentor. Quinn couldn't contain his excitement in seeing McLaurin back on the practice fields and in the meeting rooms. The Commanders need McLaurin.

The eight-year veteran is often spotted working with younger receivers after a play. It's something he enjoys. He has taken a particular interest in undrafted rookie Jaden Bradley. Last summer, even after coming off a surprising 12-5 season with high hopes, something felt off. McLaurin's absence was a big reason for those "vibes" being off. He's back. So is a healthy Daniels, and the roster has added several young and talented players this offseason. This summer, the vibes are all positive. You can see the happiness on McLaurin's face. Quinn and Daniels, too. McLaurin's impact on this franchise goes beyond the box score.

This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: 6 takeaways from first week of Commanders' training camp

title: Kelsey Plum traded to Mercury by Sparks: Trade details, what we know
description: Kelsey Plum is reportedly on the move, with the Los Angeles Sparks sending her to Phoenix.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Sparks touted the acquisition of Kelsey Plum as the dawn of a fresh competitive start. Seventeen months later, the franchise is starting over.

Los Angeles reportedly agreed to trade the five-time All-Star and two-time champion to the Phoenix Mercury on Saturday night. The move comes shortly before the WNBA trade deadline.

ESPN reported the deal yielded the Sparks guard Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round draft pick and a 2028 second-rounder in exchange for Plum.

This comes after Plum requested to be moved from the Las Vegas Aces after the 2024 season, leading to a blockbuster three-team trade including the Seattle Storm that saw the Sparks deal the No. 2 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft to secure Plum.

First-year Sparks head coach Lynne Roberts committed to a "winning season" when Plum was formally introduced in Los Angeles. The team finished the 2025 WNBA season with a 21–23 record, placing 6th in the Western Conference and missing the playoffs as Plum averaged 19.3 points per game.

The Sparks are 10-17 so far this season and fired general manager Raegan Pebley on July 12. Since then, the Sparks have lost six in a row.

Plum had not appeared in a game for the Sparks since June 21, when the Sparks beat New York 98-97 at Crypto.com Arena. The team announced that she sustained a lower left leg injury. She also suffered a right ankle sprain in late May that sidelined her for three games.

Plum was asked Thursday about the possibility of being traded, and instead pointed to the fact that she planned to play again when the Sparks visited Portland Sunday afternoon. Tip-off for that game was scheduled for 12:30 p.m. PT at Moda Center, and the trade deadline is 3 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 2.

"I'm not taking anything personal. I'm gonna be where my feet are. I play for the Sparks. So on Sunday, I'm gonna suit up," Plum said.

Instead, Plum will be preparing to suit up for a new team.

The Phoenix Mercury, which lost to the Aces in the Finals last season, have also failed to meet expectations so far this year. They have an 11-18 record, placing them 5th in the Western Conference.

title: Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes set to join Arsenal in £80m deal
description: Newcastle United have reached an agreement with Arsenal over the transfer of midfielder Bruno Guimaraes in a deal worth up to £80 million, ESPN reports.The Premier League champions have agreed to pay...
fullText:
Newcastle United have reached an agreement with Arsenal over the transfer of midfielder Bruno Guimaraes in a deal worth up to £80 million, ESPN reports.

The Premier League champions have agreed to pay an initial £70m, with a further £10m tied to performance-related bonuses.

The move is expected to be completed once the final formalities are finalised, with Guimaraes set to sign a long-term contract with the North Londoners.

The 29-year-old is also set to undergo a medical on Monday before the transfer is officially announced.

Newcastle have been picked apart this summer, with Guimaraes the latest key figure on the way out of St. James’ Park in what has been a chaotic transfer window for the Magpies.

They had already lost Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur before manager Eddie Howe’s shocking departure was announced.

With Guimaraes on his way out, Newcastle will need significant investment to rebuild an already depleted squad to boost their chances of competing at the top end of the table this season.

They’ve already sorted out their managerial dilemma, with Matthias Jassle set to replace Howe.

Guimaraes’ desire to join Arsenal reportedly played a huge role in helping the transfer move forward, while Newcastle were prepared to consider offers after missing out on Champions League football.

The Brazilian has been a talismanic figure for Newcastle since joining from Olympique Lyon in January 2022 in a deal worth around £40m.

Over the past few years, he has established himself as one of the team’s leaders and a fan favourite.

He’s also considered one of the best midfielders in the Premier League, which explains why Arsenal were ready to pay a premium fee to secure his services.

Despite missing two months of last season through injury, the Brazilian still finished as Newcastle’s top Premier League goalscorer with nine goals.

He’d become Arsenal’s third signing of the summer, following the arrivals of Greek winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge and goalkeeper Illan Meslier, who joined on a free transfer after leaving Leeds United.

title: Former Washington Women's Basketball Star Reportedly Traded to Phoenix Mercury
description: Former Huskies guard Kelsey Plum will reportedly head to her third franchise in nine years in the WNBA.
fullText:
The Washington Huskies women's basketball team has an opportunity this season to reach heights the program hasn't seen since guard Kelsey Plum was with the program.

While Plum was in the Pacific Northwest, the Huskies made the NCAA tournament multiple times and made their first (and only) Final Four appearance in 2016.

Plum was not only the best player on Washington during that stretch, but was one of the best players in the nation during that stretch. She was a several-time all-conference selection and was a consensus All-American in 2017. The same season, she was named the Pac-12 Player of the Year and the Associated Press Player of the Year.

Plum parlayed that success into being the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 WNBA Draft, and has been one of the most recognizable and well-decorated players in the Association since.

In her nine years in WNBA with the San Antonio Stars/Las Vegas Aces and Los Angeles Sparks, Plum is a two-time champion (2022-23), five-time All-Star (2022-26), one-time Sixth Player of the Year (2021) and one-time All-WNBA first-team selection ('22).

The one accolade that has eluded the former Husky in her career has been a regular season MVP. In the first half of the season, it seemed like Plum had a chance to obtain that trophy.

In 12 games this season, Plum has averaged 23.9 points per game on 52.7% shooting from the floor (38.3% shooting from 3-point range). She's also averaged 6.4 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.2 steals per contest while turning the ball over just 3.2 times on average.

Kelsey Plum tonight 🔥

• 25 points 
• 4 assists 
• 9/16 FG pic.twitter.com/wLcbbThM4B

— Women’s Hoops Network (@WomensHoops_USA) May 14, 2026

Plum's MVP-caliber season has been derailed by a soft tissue injury in her leg. She missed the last 11 games for the Sparks due to the ailment and was unable to participate in the All-Star Game on July 25. Los Angeles went 2-9 in the 11 games Plum missed.

It's been reported for several days by various sources that the New York Liberty, Atlanta Dream and Phoenix Mercury were interested in acquiring the five-time All-Star.

Per a report on "X" from ESPN insiders Shams Charania and Kendra Andrews, the Mercury won out on the Plum sweepstakes and acquired Plum from Los Angeles in return for second-year guard Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round WNBA draft pick and a 2028 second-round draft pick.

Despite Plum's injury, it might not be soon before Plum makes her debut in a Phoenix uniform. Per a report on "X" from ESPN's Alexa Philippou, Plum was expected to play on a minute restriction for the Sparks if she wasn't dealt by the trade deadline Sunday.

title: “There’s Been a Narrative”: Aaron Rodgers Explains Wife’s Role in Helping Him Reconnect With Family After Years of Separation
description: Aaron Rodgers’s relationship with his family was strained for several years. However, the quarterback reconnected with his parents and siblings during the offseason.
fullText:
Aaron Rodgers’s relationship with his family was strained for several years. However, the quarterback reconnected with his parents and siblings during the offseason.

In an interview with NFL Network’s Kyle Brandt on Saturday, Rodgers credited his wife for helping him make amends with his family. The four-time NFL MVP said the urge to repair his relationship with his family grew after he got married.

“A big part of it was getting married,” Rodgers said. “Having those conversations with my wife that allowed me to open up to the possibility of coming together. It’s been a couple-year process now, the conversations with them. I’ve been very closed off about that part of my life, and I want to keep it that way. But there’s been a narrative going on for too long that I wanted to shut down.”

Rodgers said that he was happy to reunite with his family.

“That part of my life is A really beautiful addition, and I got to give my wife a lot of credit. Not that she was pushing me, because she never was. But just the way she loves and supports me, having her by my side during this process was really special.

“I missed those relationships. And there was reasons that don’t need to be talked about, but I’m thankful that’s come all the way back around.”

Last month, Rodgers shared photos of himself with his parents and brother Luke in Nashville, Tennessee. However, the quarterback’s other brother, Jordan, was missing from the pictures.

According to a report by People in 2024, Rodgers had been estranged from his parents and brothers for close to a decade.

Rodgers reportedly married a woman named Brittani in June 2025. He was seen wearing a wedding band during last year’s Kentucky Derby. However, information about his wife remains scarce, as she stays away from the limelight.

During an appearance on the “Pat McAfee Show” last June, the four-time NFL MVP said he wishes to keep his private life private.

After the 2025 season, speculation was rife about Aaron Rodgers’ possible retirement. However, the quarterback has returned to the Pittsburgh Steelers for another year.

Rodgers clarified that this would be his final year in the league. While speaking with Kyle Brandt, he further clarified his stance.

“It’s been that way for the last couple Of years,” Rodgers said. “I kind of had shut this door 99%. And then Mike (McCarthy) got hired. He kind of put his foot in the door a little bit.

“I just wanted to start the relationship up again. … I’m real glad to be back.”

Rodgers also denied the possibility of playing another year if he finds success with the Steelers in 2026. Last season, he helped the team make the playoffs as the AFC North winners. However, they lost to the Texans in a wild-card showdown.

According to Diario SPORT, Ajax have made a loan proposal with an option to buy for Torrents, which is currently being evaluated at the Barcelona offices.

The full-back is one of La Masia’s brightest jewels, a left-back tipped for an important role in the future, but one who needs regular minutes to continue his development.

As such, a departure this summer looks all but certain, with the youngster having received numerous offers from both Spain and across Europe. His future is expected to be resolved next week.

The specifics of Ajax’s proposal are particularly interesting. The Dutch club would take Torrens on loan while covering his full salary, along with an option to buy 50% of his rights for €5 million.

Barcelona would be able to buy that percentage back in the future, allowing them to retain control over the youngster while generating a small profit in the process.

Barcelona are expected to retain a buyback clause. (Photo by Rafa Babot/Getty Images)

Barcelona are increasingly prioritising sales with buy-back clauses to extract value from their assets while they develop elsewhere.

It is worth noting that Barcelona held onto several of their young players this summer specifically to complete a squad without internationals during pre-season, allowing Hansi Flick to assess them at close quarters.

Now, a number of those departures are expected to gather pace.

Ajax’s interest is not limited to Torrens either, with the Dutch side also said to have enquired about defender Landry Farre.

Ultimately, the decision will rest with Torrens and the club, but all signs point towards a move that suits both parties.

The player would gain the game time he craves, while Barcelona would preserve the option of bringing him back should his career continue on its upward trajectory.

title: Wirtz: “[Liverpool] Have a Lot of Things to Do Better”
description: Liverpool’s German wunderkind has joined the club for pre-season and shared a few thoughts on the pending campaign.
fullText:
Liverpool’s pre-season is in proper gear with news of a few of the World Cup participants beginning to filter back into the club’s preparations. Among the group rejoining is German international, Florian Wirtz. The attacking midfielder had a disappointing World Cup campaign, with the German side getting knocked out in the Round of 32 – coincidentally eliminated on the same day as his Liverpool teammates on the Netherlands.

Now, he’ll look to shake the truncated tournament run and look to improve upon an inaugural season on Merseyside that some – not me – would label a disappointment. That begins now as the attacking star has begun preparations and is expected to figure in the pre-season match against Leeds on Sunday.

Speaking to the official site on Friday, Wirtz expressed some thoughts regarding last year.

“Yeah, of course I wasn’t happy at all – about the season, I mean. I was not unhappy every day when I came to training, but I think we expected much more last season. I think we start from zero this season. Also here with this training camp, it’s a new start. We have a lot of things to do better this season and I’m very excited for season two.”

While I can understand that folks found his debut disappointing, I thought there were some mitigating circumstances to temper some of that. First and most importantly, there was a marked improvement during the second half of the season, with Wirtz managing to find more opportunities to work a breakthrough and either provide an assist or latch onto the end of a movement to notch a goal. There was always going to be a bit of an adjustment period for anyone moving from the Bundesliga to the Premier League and the most heartening thing about his performances last year is that they tended to improve over time.

Besides that, the injuries to the attackers around him – namely to Alexander Isak and eventually to Hugo Ekitike – meant that the players that might have provided him the kind of support to force defenders out of space simply weren’t available. On top of that, Arne Slot simply couldn’t figure out the right combination of players or tactics to make use of such a talented roster. It was a collective disappointment and I’d personally stop short of going full-send on applying that label to Wirtz.

But there’s not two ways about it: this year needs to be better.

That’s why it’s so encouraging to see Wirtz in camp and ready to put in the work. Hopefully the short break means he’s coming in sharper and more ready to come good on all of the promise that Liverpool brass invested so heavily in.

title: A's Could Pursue High-Upside Reclamation in Former Top St. Louis Cardinals Prospect
description: Hence was a consensus top-100 prospect as recently as 2025. Now available, the 23-year-old right-hander represents the kind of calculated bet the A's have made work before — and need to make again
fullText:
The A's have had a knack for bringing in guys with command issues and giving them a shot to have success. It's not very often that those players were top-100 prospects as recently as the previous season.

That is the situation the A's could find themselves in with right-hander Tink Hence, who was designated for assignment by the St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday. Hence was a second-round selection in the 2020 MLB Draft, and was a consensus top-100 prospect from 2023-25, reaching as high as No. 38 according to Baseball Prospectus before the 2025 campaign.

When the A's were looking to trade Sean Murphy after the 2022 season, Hence was a prospect that was put in a lot of hypothetical trade packages. He's had the talent for a while, but he's still looking to make it click.

The 23-year-old has been sidelined by injuries, including a lat strain, chest tightness, and shoulder problems. He was only able to accumulate 21 ⅓ innings last season, half of which came in Double-A, though he made eight starts and held a 2.95 ERA. Up until this season, when he'd been healthy, he'd been productive.

This season he has racked up 20 ⅓ innings and holds a 6.64 ERA while pitching in Triple-A Memphis for the first time. He's also been largely pitching in relief, making 19 appearances with three outings serving as the opener.

His strikeout rate — which has hit above 30% a number of times in his minor-league journey — has slumped to 20.2% this season out of the bullpen, while his walk rate has been an unsustainable 18.2%.

Given that he's already been DFA'd, there will be teams clamoring for their own shot and making things click with Hence. He's still young, and certainly has the skills to succeed. There is some risk involved here, because an acquiring team will likely be bidding against other clubs for Hence, but for the A's, that risk is worth it.

He represents the kind of post-hype, high-upside arm that the club needs more of in the farm system. While the injuries are a concern, Hence's two option years (2026, 2027) do create some time for the A's to try him as a starting pitcher again. By 2028, he'd be out of options, forcing a decision on his future with the club.

Hence's circle change is his best weapon, and helps him achieve a 45.6% ground-ball rate. Kade Morris (56.1%), Joel Kuhnel (48.8%), and J.T. Ginn (46.8%) are the only pitchers with the A's this season with a higher ground ball rate.

They could have him start in Midland, get settled, then move up to Las Vegas for the real test. If things don't go well, then he could go back to relief work, where the A's could also use some help.

For the A's, Hence represents a calculated bet on a pitcher who still has time to deliver on his prospect pedigree. The window for him is narrow, but at 23 with at least a pair of high-end offerings, the righty has the stuff to be another reclamation success story.

title: Phillies Trade Rumors: Challenges Ahead After Tarik Skubal Blockbuster
description: The Philadelphia Phillies could face new challenges after losing out on the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes. The post Phillies Trade Rumors: Challenges Ahead After Tarik Skubal Blockbuster appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Though the Philadelphia Phillies were seen as a long-shot contender to land pitcher Tarik Skubal, his deal to the Los Angeles Dodgers could create new challenges for the NL East contenders.

The Dodgers reportedly landed the Detroit Tigers ace in a trade reported in the late hours on Saturday, a move that is expected to have a domino effect on the rest of the trade market. That could complicate plans for the Phillies, who likely remain in the market for starting pitching help after losing out on Skubal.

Before Saturday’s trade was finalized, MLB.com reporter Mark Feinsand noted that the rest of the baseball world was left in a holding pattern.

“The Dodgers, Brewers, Rays, Braves and Cubs are widely viewed as the five most likely landing spots for Skubal, with the Yankees and Phillies among the other interested (but less likely) suitors,” Feinsand reported. “Until a Skubal trade happens — and multiple executives donât believe it will until Sunday night or Monday morning — the rest of the starting pitching market could be in a holding pattern.”

Skubal’s trade could now unlock the next level of trade targets, with the Phillies likely looking at some of them.

“That is the likely scenario, one NL executive said, ‘at least for the upper-end guys,’ ” the report noted. “That would mean Kevin Gausman, Mize, Clay Holmes, Robbie Ray and Peralta. Other starters with expiring contracts who could be moved include Brady Singer, Shane Bieber and Foster Griffin, though Griffin started for Washington on Friday as the Nationals contemplate whether to buy or sell.”

But Skubal’s trade could also loosen the rest of the market. One MLB insider told Feinsand that prior to the Skubal trade, teams were setting high asking prices for rental players and not yet ready to back off.

âSellers are holding high and buyers are balking,” the exec said. âThat has to change at some point this weekend, doesnât it?â

Before the Saturday trade, MLB.com writer Thomas Harrigan ranked the Phillies at No. 6 on the list of teams that needed him the most. Harrigan noted that Skubal was more of a want than a need for the Phillies, but still could have put the team over the top.

“The Phillies donât have a glaring need in their rotation, but there may not be many ceiling-raisers out there at Philadelphiaâs other positions of need,” Harrigan wrote. “And for a club with an aging core that hasnât been able to get over the hump, the idea of going into the playoffs with a rotation of Skubal, Cristopher SÃ¡nchez, Zack Wheeler and JesÃºs Luzardo is hard to dismiss.”

But Harrigan questioned whether the Phillies were already near their ceiling for contention.

“Adding Skubal would shore up their standing in the NL playoff race, but their chances of earning a bye are slim,” Harrigan wrote. “That means they could have to win three playoff rounds against some combination of the Dodgers, Brewers, Braves and Cubs — four teams theyâve gone 5-17 against in 2026 — just to get to the Fall Classic. Itâs going to be a tall task, even if they had a super rotation.”

title: Chelsea 1–2 Tottenham Hotspur: Three talking points
description: What when wrong and what went right against Chelsea?
fullText:
Editor’s note: As mentioned in the match report yesterday, in a departure from our usual structure I’ve elaborated on some talking points based on observations I made at the ground as well as a match report; as such, I’ve done some deeper analysis rather than the high-level talking points we might typically cover.

Tottenham Hotspur concluded their Antipodean tour with a last-gasp victory against London rivals Chelsea in front of a packed house at Accor Stadium in Sydney. Strong sides named by Roberto De Zerbi and Xabi Alonso brought an intensity to the match not yet seen this preseason, with both sides balancing desire for victory with the need to focus on preparations for the upcoming season.

Any best-laid plans went out the window though as Kevin Danso was red carded in the first half while scores were level, causing a change in approach for both teams. Chelsea tried to make their numbers advantage count, but it was Spurs who came out on top 2-1 as Richarlison knocked in a dramatic late winner.

Here’s a deep dive into a few things I took away from Spurs’ final Australian preseason fixture.

There’s a reason rival sides typically don’t play each other in preseason (though it is starting to happen more and more thanks to $$$). Preseason is supposed to be about fitness, tactics, and getting a look at the players in the wider squad; not about winning – though that is sometimes an added bonus. Introducing a rivalry changes all of that, with fans and players alike strongly motivated to push for victory, even at the expense of preparation.

There was a strong feeling in the crowd as the different groups of fans traded off songs and boos as players were announced, and once the match kicked off it was clear the fixture would be anything but friendly. The referee swallowed his whistle early on as Spurs were on the receiving end of a couple of robust tackles, and that lack of control by the officials very quickly allowed things to escalate with Spurs largely being the ones driving the provocation.

A robust challenge by Marco Palestra on Gallagher signified the start of the lift in intensity, before Dominic Solanke left an elbow on Levi Colwill as he pressured the center back. Jan Paul van Hecke clearly relished the physicality as well, making it his personal mission to marshal Joao Pedro, going in hard on the Brazilian on a couple of occasions before Andy Robertson also clattered Palestra. There were questions levied at Alasdair Gold by some of the Chelsea press along the lines of, “What’s wrong with Spurs?” as the Lilywhites clearly played aggressor, letting their frustrations out on the opposition players (his response was, “They’re just letting the Chelsea players know they’re there!”).

That all came to a head when Conor Gallagher went in heavily on Dario Essugo late and with two feet. It was a challenge that was arguably one of those “orange card” situations, the only thing saving the Englishman the lack of studs-up contact and the friendly nature of the encounter (which had gone down the drain approximately 30 minutes earlier). There was a coming together from both teams with pushing and shoving and finger pointing – a clash full of sound and fury, signifying nothing.

On any other day, things could have escalated further from there, and in some ways they did, as Kevin Danso was shown a red card early in the second half as he clumsily let a back pass run before dragging down Pedro, who was through on goal. That expulsion though actually caused the intensity to deflate like a balloon, with Spurs forced to play on the back foot and keep things tight, and the players noticeably less willing to dive in to compete for 50-50 challenges.

That threw a spanner in the works for the preparations for both sides, but in some ways was a good thing: the way events had been progressing in the first half it felt like injuries were inevitable as both sides took pot shots at opposition ankles. That’s exactly what you don’t want in preseason, and it’s why you don’t want to line up rivals for these fixtures. The desire to compete and win can override any sense of self-preservation and then you end up with injured players going into the season.

No thanks (even though I acknowledge that it was an incredible experience for the fans!)

At the risk of a spoiler alert, the answer to that question is a resounding no.

Archie Gray’s positional flexibility has been both a blessing and a curse in his Spurs career up until this point. He has a fantastic football IQ and decent technical skills, allowing him to slot into almost any position and make a good fist of it. Unfortunately, that has come at the cost of dedicated development in any of those roles. Thankfully, last season we saw Gray begin to settle into more of a consistent role in the middle of the park and the young Englishman start to show glimpses of the player he could become.

Spurs, though, still have a depth issue at fullback, one that has been exacerbated on this tour due to the unavailability of Djed Spence and Pedro Porro (World Cup duties), as well as Destiny Udogie (injury). This has meant a heavy reliance on academy players Tye Hall and Rio Kyerematen, ostensibly central midfielders, to deputize in those roles; but against Chelsea, it was clear Roberto De Zerbi wanted more experience in that position: hence, Archie Gray back at right back once more.

Deploying midfielders in the fullback roles is something De Zerbi has utilized quite frequently on previous occasions, especially at Brighton & Hove Albion, where he at times would line up Pascal Gross or Jack Hinshelwood in inverted roles. The thinking is that their relative level of technical ability on the ball compared to a standard fullback allows them to tuck in and act as another press resistant ball recipient in the middle of the park, enabling further fluid rotations as part of the third man build-up tactic, and drawing defenses out of shape. It’s also a role Rio Kyerematen (who, like I mentioned above, is a midfielder) performed exceedingly well against Sydney FC in midweek.

For Gray, though, it didn’t quite work. Lucas Bergvall often ended up drifting into the right-side half-spaces due to Conor Gallagher dropping deep on the left, leaving limited space for Gray to utilize in possession, and going forward he struggled to create space for attacking passes and crosses around the box. Additionally, Jamie Gittens, Jorrel Hato, and Joao Pedro often worked in tandem to overload Spurs’ right edge with Gray given limited support by Solomon in defense, pinning Spurs’ captain back in his defensive third.

Gittens and Pedro especially gave Gray a torrid time, often getting past him easily on a number of occasions that Spurs were lucky did not result in Chelsea goals. Thankfully, late on Gray was shifted into the center of the pitch as Tye Hall and Rio Kyerematen were brought on, and immediately looked miles more comfortable. His positioning and anticipation were key to breaking up a number of Chelsea attacks, and his willingness to both disrupt the Chelsea buildup and look forward in attack were core to Spurs’ winning goal.

It’s nice for Archie to have a few strings to his bow, and I’m sure he’ll get called upon to fill various roles where needed as the season progresses; but here’s hoping he can see more time in the middle of the park. It’s there where his future lies, and he’s been excellent there through preseason thus far.

Look, it feels a little pessimistic to focus on the negative areas of what was really an impressive Spurs performance. There are plenty of positive takeaways: Hardy and Kyerematen were fantastic once more, as was Mathys Tel; Jan Paul van Hecke and Ben Davies were solid in defense; and Antonin Kinsky put in an heroic performance between the posts. It was also a fantastic, backs-against-the-wall performance with ten men, from which Spurs somehow secured a win against Chelsea with a 90th minute winner. That doesn’t often happen!

That said, there were a few shaky performances as well. As mentioned in my match report, Sandro Tonali looks far from a £100 million player. Let’s start with the positives: his goal was well struck; his movement was good; and his defensive positioning was generally excellent. Unfortunately, there were quite a few negatives, one of which was his touch, which was atrociously heavy for a central midfielder in Roberto De Zerbi’s system. He struggled receiving the ball under pressure, and his passing limitations were clear to see.

At times, he was guilty of trying to do too much as well, at one point dribbling into the midst of four Chelsea players in a moment you could clearly see was a disaster waiting to happen. Sure enough, he was dispossessed (though arguably by being fouled) and Estevao was one on one with Kinsky. It’s early on in his Spurs career, but you do expect more; will he succumb to the pressure of the price tag? Maybe I’m being too harsh (he wasn’t the worst on the pitch by far), but that’s the criticism his transfer fee will engender.

And that takes us to two other poor performers, and my main point: Andy Robertson and Dominic Solanke. Both put in absolute stinkers on the pitch, and for both it was their first start of the tour – so what do these performances tell us really? Are these performances lacking due to lack of player quality / form; or is it just shaking off the rust, and we can expect more once the season begins?

Robertson really struggled in possession. He made a couple of awful passes that created attacks from nothing for Chelsea, and though he was generally solid defensively down his edge, his losing of both Estevao and the flight of the ball for Chelsea’s goal was woefully poor defending. His crossing and passing around the box however was a positive, but he will need to offer more than that to be at a level Spurs need; especially given Destiny Udogie’s injury record and Djed Spence’s limitations in build-up on the left.

As for Solanke, he was… a non-entity. So much so, in fact, that when after a 90th minute winner and close to 45 minutes defending with only ten men, the press corps were informed he would be the player interviewed at the post-match press conference, there was an audible groan. His touch was that of late-stage Emmanuel Adebayor, and the things he is supposed to be good at (pressing, hold-up, and linking with attackers) was almost non-existent; Richarlison, for whom these are not typically strengths, outperformed the Englishman. It’s a real fall from grace for a striker who just recently was Spurs’ record signing.

As I said above, though, the hope is that these are teething problems, and just a case of preseason rust. After all, there’s only so much you can read into these performances. Can they step up when the need arises?

Screw it, we’re gonna win the league.

title: Yoshinobu Yamamoto Reacts to Dodgers’ Blockbuster Tarik Skubal Trade
description: As many expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers pulled off a blockbuster trade to acquire Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal on Saturday night. The package heading to Detroit included outfielder Zyhir Hope, MLB’s No. 25 prospect, right-handed pitcher River Ryan, and right-handed pitcher Brady Smith. Yoshinobu Yamamoto Reacts to Trade Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto took the […] The post Yoshinobu Yamamoto Reacts to Dodgers’ Blockbuster Tarik Skubal Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
As many expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers pulled off a blockbuster trade to acquire Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal on Saturday night.

The package heading to Detroit included outfielder Zyhir Hope, MLB’s No. 25 prospect, right-handed pitcher River Ryan, and right-handed pitcher Brady Smith.

Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto took the mound against the Boston Red Sox on Saturday and tossed eight innings despite the team’s 3-2 loss.

Shortly after the trade became official, reporters asked Yamamoto for his reaction. He kept his response brief, admitting he was surprised after hearing rumors that the deal could materialize.

“I was hearing some rumors about that, but then it actually happened. I’m pretty surprised,” Yamamoto said through an interpreter.

“I was hearing some rumors about that, but then it actually happened. I’m pretty surprised.”

Yoshinobu Yamamoto (L (11-7), 8.0 IP, 4 H, 3 ER, BB, 3 K, 96 P) talks with the media on the #Dodgers reportedly acquiring back-to-back AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal via tradeâ¦ pic.twitter.com/SQWWCD40Wn

â SportsNet LA (@SportsNetLA) August 2, 2026

The Dodgers now boast what could become one of the most talented starting rotations not only in MLB today, but in baseball history.

Several pitchers are currently on the injured list, and Shohei Ohtani is not pitching as he continues to recover from a lingering knee injury. However, once everyone is healthy, the Dodgers’ five- or six-man rotation could look like this:

Blake Snell (2.35 ERA last season, currently on the injured list)

Tyler Glasnow (2.72 ERA, currently on the injured list)

That doesn’t even include Roki Sasaki, Emmet Sheehan, and Eric Lauer, all of whom have made meaningful contributions to the Dodgers’ pitching staff this season.

After dropping their second straight game on Saturday night, the Dodgers are 68-42 and now trail the Milwaukee Brewers (69-41) by a half-game for the best record in baseball.

Los Angeles is looking to become the first team since the New York Yankees (1998-2000) to win three consecutive World Series titles. The Dodgers already entered the postseason as heavy favorites, and adding Skubal only strengthens their chances.
